notes: Warning messages (0x20, 0x21, 0x37) carry a 1-byte VTEC event code at byte 1 (see 'events'); severity is implied by the significance letter. 0 = unknown event.

space_weather.layout: 0:type 1-4:issued_unix_min u32 5:kp24h*3 6-8:kp_day1..3*3 9:G1<<4|G2 10:G3<<4 11-13:S1+% 14-16:R1-R2% 17-19:R3+% 20-21:sfi u16 22-23:ssn u16(0xFFFF=unknown) 24:xray class*10+mag(255=unknown) 25:kp_now<<4|kp_expected (observed K from ALTKnn, expected K from WARKnn or watch G+4; 0=none) 26:xray_alert<<4|proton_alert (xray 1=R2 M5+, 2=R3 X1+ within 3h; proton 1=S1 expected, 2=S1 observed, 3=S2+ observed)

bot.note: first two bytes of the bot public key

type.note: high nibble = message type, low nibble = flags; flags bits 2-3 are the data source in every type but cancel

v5.notes: MeshWX v5 (spec 5.0). Every message is the data field of one MeshCore GRP_DATA packet on #meshwx with data_type 0xFF10, at most 165 bytes. All multi-byte integers are little-endian; times are Unix minutes as u32. The type byte is (type << 4) | flags. Warnings are keyed by (event, office, etn), not by seq. Coverage (type 8, spec 7A) is the bot's own statement of what it carries: centre, radius in km, office indices, and its zones as the same UGC runs a warning's area list uses; a set flag means that list was cut, so a code missing from it means 'not stated', never 'not covered'. Never infer a bot's coverage from the stations or warnings you happen to have received. Revision 5 adds two times, both appended after everything a revision 4 decoder reads, both announced by a flags-nibble bit. Warning flag 2: two more bytes, a u16 of the minutes between the product's issuance and 'expires', so issued = expires - that; show it as 'issued', never as when the packet arrived. Observations flag 1: ceil(n / 2) more bytes, one nibble per station in 10-minute steps (station i in the low nibble of byte i div 2 when i is even, the high nibble when odd, 15 = 150 minutes or more), saying how much older than 'ts' that station's own METAR is; show 'as of ts - age' per station, and stale is measured from that, not from 'ts'. A batch with ages carries at most 13 stations. Indices into offices/stations/states come from index.json; event codes from 'events' and sky codes from 'sky_codes' in this file. The v3/v4 keys above are retained for legacy clients and are unrelated to v5. Revision 6 adds Request (type 9, spec 7B), the one message that travels app -> bot: a `>` request flooded on the same channel as a GRP_DATA datagram. Body: 6 bytes of the sender's public key (the prefix a DM identifies the same phone by), a u32 LE of the sender's own Unix SECONDS (not minutes), then the `>` text, UTF-8, at most 40 bytes, ending the packet. `bot` names the bot asked; 65535 asks them all, and a bot ignores a request naming another bot. The answer is unchanged: the bot's normal flooded v5 messages, to everyone. Revision 7 adds a data source and a text cut flag, and moves no byte. The source is bits 2-3 of the flags nibble ('source' above: mask 12, shift 2) and means where the weather in this message came from: 0 unstated, 1 received off the GOES satellite by the bot's own dish, 2 fetched from NOAA over the internet, 3 built from products of both kinds. It is the same two bits in every type but one. Cancel (type 2) is the exception and always will be: its whole nibble is a reason code, so never read a source out of a cancel and never write one into it. Request, Not available and Coverage carry 0: they are not built from a weather product, and Coverage describes the bot's own configuration. 0 is also what every pre-revision-7 bot sends, so read it as the absence of a claim, never as a claim of absence. Text flag 1 ('cut'): the product was longer than eight chunks and the tail was dropped. It is set on EVERY chunk of a cut reply, so losing the last packet does not lose the fact; the text still ends at a sentence, is never cut inside a word, and carries no ellipsis. Show it as an excerpt with a way to ask the bot again, not as a transmission fault. Revision 8 changes one answer and no byte: `>o ICAO` for a station with no fresh report answers with the nearest station within 40 km of it that has one, as a batch of one under THAT station's index; Not available only when nothing within 40 km reports. Match it to the request by distance from the station you named, from the bot you asked, and file it under the index it carries. Revision 9 adds Area sweep (type 10, spec 7C): the national picture of active alerts, as runs of UGC numbers a phone draws on its own bundled outlines. Body: 'built' u32 LE Unix minutes when the bot built it, 'group' u8 (the same on every packet of one sweep, the seq its first packet went out with, as Text does), 'idx' u8 from 0, 'total' u8 1 to 8, then 4-byte entries, at most 38 a packet. One entry is one run of consecutive UGC numbers in one state: 'event' u8 (the same event codes a Warning uses, the most severe event covering the run), then state << 1 | kind (state index in bits 1-7, bit 0: 0 forecast zone Z, 1 county C), then a u16 LE holding the start number in bits 0-9 and run - 1 in bits 10-15, so a run is 1 to 64 numbers. This is NOT the Warning area run: that one spends a whole byte on the run and flags a county in bit 7. Entries are ordered most severe first, then by state, then by start. Flag 1 ('cut'): entries were dropped because the sweep did not fit in eight packets, set on EVERY packet; the ones dropped are the least severe. Flag 2 ('advisories'): advisories and statements (VTEC significance Y and S) are included as well as warnings and watches; without it an area absent from the sweep may still hold an advisory. Reassemble by (bot, group) in idx order, and read a sweep as a picture built at 'built', not as a live feed. It answers `>wmap` (`>wmap all` for the advisories) and is never broadcast on a schedule: at most one sweep every 5 minutes across all senders, and only when a whole one still fits in the bot's hourly packet budget. A request inside either limit is answered Not available, reason 4. Revision 10 adds three request forms and reinterprets one byte. `>part <group> <idx>[,<idx>...]` asks for the named packets of a multi-packet answer again, an Area sweep or a Text, by the 'group' byte those packets carry. The bot keeps the transmitted bytes of its last 8 multi-packet answers ('limits.parts_cache_groups') for 600 seconds ('limits.parts_cache_seconds'), keyed by the group as stamped at transmission, and sends the named packets again: identical bytes except a new seq, so a resent packet keeps the group it was assembled under and a phone still reassembles by (bot, group). Not available, request letter 'p', reason 0 when the bot no longer holds that group or none of the indexes exist in it. Each resent packet comes out of the hourly budget and the per-sender 5 s rule applies; the sweep cooldown neither applies nor restarts, because a resend is not a new sweep. The same (group, idx) is resent at most once every 30 seconds ('limits.part_resend_floor_seconds') whoever asks, so ten phones missing the same packet cost one packet; a request whose every index is inside that window gets nothing at all, which is not an error. `>wmap [all] [states]` scopes the sweep: up to 15 ('limits.sweep_scope_states') two-letter codes from index.json 'states', run together or separated by spaces or commas, in any case. No states is the whole country, as in revision 9. An unknown code is Not available reason 1. 'all' is the advisories level and is matched as a whole token, never Alabama plus a stray letter; 'ALLA' is four characters and so is Alabama and Louisiana. A scoped sweep sets bit 7 of 'total' ('area_sweep.scoped_bit') on EVERY packet, so a phone that lost packet 0 still knows it is not looking at the country, and the packet count is what is left under 'area_sweep.total_mask'. Packet 0 of a scoped sweep begins with one scope entry per state asked for: event 0 ('area_sweep.scope_event'; no event has code 0), zone kind, start 0, run 1, which is XXZ000, the Weather Service's own way of writing 'all of state XX'. Scope entries sort before every alert entry and count toward the 38 a packet holds. A state named in the scope with no alert entries behind it has nothing active at that level: that is an answer, and the reason the scope is on the wire at all. The sweep cooldown is per state from revision 10: a request is refused with reason 4 when every state it names was covered in the last 5 minutes at the same or a higher level ('all' is higher than plain), and a national request when a national sweep at that level went out in the last 5 minutes. `>f <lat>,<lon>` asks for a forecast at a coordinate in decimal degrees, the app sending 3 decimals. It is recognised by the comma between two signed decimals and answered exactly as a resolved place is: the nearest point the bot holds a forecast for, under that point's bundle index, or 65535 when the point is not in the bundle. Out of range is Not available reason 1. The one byte revision 10 reinterprets is 'total': revision 9 wrote all eight bits but never a value above 8, so a revision 9 sweep reads the same under the mask, and no revision 9 client had shipped.
